title: I may have gotten smart mesh deformation working on 3D models...
author: Crockiestar
selftext:
If you’ve ever tried to move a 3D model with no rig, skinning, or weight painting, you know how much work stands between you and a simple pose. I wanted it to feel as immediate as moving pins in 2D. [Monster Mash](https://monstermash.zone/) was a big inspiration.

So I started experimenting, and I think I’ve got it working. With Warp 3D, you upload a model, place a few pins, and start moving it. Smooth ARAP deformation over a voxelized volume makes the mesh follow, and the timeline automatically fills in the movement between poses. There’s inverse kinematics too, so you can move a paw or hand and have the limb follow.

I honestly think this solves the “I just want to move this model” problem. When you’re done, you can export an **animated GLB or glTF**, export the **current pose as a GLB**, or save an editable Warp 3D project.

AI is optional: you can refine animations using a Gemini API key or sign in with ChatGPT to use your Codex subscription (beta). The desktop app also supports MCP, so you can connect your own compatible AI agent to control the editor.

The video shows it in action. Enjoy!

  
Try it here [Warp Studio](https://crockiestar.itch.io/warp-studio)

replies.author: Crockiestar
replies.body: A Blender lattice is basically a cage you manually deform around the mesh. Warp 3D uses pins and ARAP, so for example if you pin a creature’s shoulder and drag its hand upward, the limb can naturally curve and redistribute the deformation instead of you having to manually shape that bend with a cage.

comments.author: Jestersheepy
comments.body:
I don't get it.

The UX between using a rig or using pins is the same? Using a rig with controllers setup has far higher quality results and with a lot of AI tools these days you can auto rig and auto skin.   
As for animation, the 2D graph curves in most modelling software gives you, again, much higher quality and control? 

I don't know what problem this app is trying to solve?

replies.author: Crockiestar
replies.body:
You’re not wrong a proper rig will give you more control and higher quality results the more detail you add to it. I plan on adding more in depth controls for advanced detailed animations soon. This tool is more about being able to move a model like a puppet as fast and easily as possible. If you open a model and just want to move a limb, bend the body, or pose it. Or make a quick animation this is the fastest and easiest way to do it. You can even adjust the strength slider to to how rigid or loose you want the object to deform as you pull on stuff. you should be able to do that immediately without rigging and weight painting / skinning first. 

I definitely think more 3D tools will adopt this specific smart ARAP voxel deformation as a tool on the toolbar as it works a lot better than you would expect I personally think it should be the default tool when you open a model in something like blender.
